rachel (sec-eng): Heads-up — noticed certificate propagation SLOs spiked for apac yesterday after the RBAC cleanup. Auditbot shows a bunch of KMS decrypt DENY entries for the proxy keystore. Can someone surface the likely root? :eyes:

omar (infra): Seen the DENYs too. RBAC change last Thursday tightened the keystore role scope. I suspect service account token used by the cert-propagator lost kms:Decrypt on a subset of key aliases.
sree (sre): Can you paste an example log? Need to know which alias and which principal.
rachel (sec-eng): Sure — grabbed an example from apac-proxy-01:

```
ERROR 2026-03-20T22:41:02Z cert-propagator: decrypt failed alias/redwood-proxy-apac: AccessDeniedException: User arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/provisioner-role/apac-propagator is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource alias/redwood-proxy-apac (status=403)
```

rachel (sec-eng): Auditbot timeline: many of these start ~22:30 UTC and correspond to a slow rollout of the RBAC policy change.
auditbot: NOTE: 37 DENY events observed for principal provisioner-role/apac-propagator between 2026-03-20T22:28Z and 2026-03-20T23:05Z. Related change: iam-policy/keystore-restrict-2026-03-20 applied to group infra-provisioners.

anna (platform): The policy intended to limit keystore *writes* only; reads (kms:Decrypt) should have been preserved. Looks like a wildcard alias condition in the policy accidentally omitted apac aliases. I'll pull the policy diff. :mag_right:
omar (infra): If that's the case, two quick mitigations: roll back the policy patch to the prior version (fast), or attach an explicit kms:Decrypt allow for `alias/redwood-proxy-apac` to the provisioner-role (surgical). Which do we want?
sree (sre): Rollback gets us immediate SLO recovery; surgical patch is safer long-term but slower to validate. What are constraints for cert rotation during rollback? We risk letting previous broader permissions remain.
rachel (sec-eng): We should also verify audit logging for post-incident window. Need to ensure deny events are retained and exported to our long-term SIEM. auditbot, confirm retention for apac DENY logs >= 30d?
auditbot: CONFIRM: DENY events for KMS are logged to cloud-audit:keystore and forwarded to SIEM with 90d retention. Last export successful at 2026-03-20T23:10Z.

anna (platform): Policy diff:
```
- "Resource": ["arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:alias/redwood-proxy-*"]
+ "Resource": ["arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:alias/redwood-proxy-*"]
+ // OOPS missing apac region alias list (alias/redwood-proxy-apac)
```

anna (platform): Summary: the change inadvertently scoped only us-west aliases. I can push a targeted fix to include the apac alias in 5–10m.
omar (infra): I'm +1 for surgical fix. I'll stand by to validate. Can we also confirm cert-propagator retries/backoff didn't exhaust our issuance window?
sree (sre): Check looks ok — propagator retried for ~12m and queued some certs, which caused the SLO breach but not a full outage. Queue depth peaked at 120 tasks.
rachel (sec-eng): Action items:
- anna: push targeted policy patch adding `alias/redwood-proxy-apac` and include an integration test for region wildcarding. (ETA 10m)
- omar: prepare rollback plan if patch fails.
- sree: validate propagator queue drain and confirm no cert expirations missed.
- platform + sec: update runbook to include a preflight that checks alias coverage after RBAC edits.

keystore-bot: POLICY PATCH applied to iam-policy/keystore-restrict-2026-03-20: added resource arn:aws:kms:apac-1:123456789012:alias/redwood-proxy-apac (applied by anna@redwood).

anna (platform): Pushed. Running quick smoke: `aws kms decrypt --key-id alias/redwood-proxy-apac --ciphertext-blob fileb://test.ct` returned success.
omar (infra): Validated from apac-proxy-01: `kubectl exec -n certs cert-propagator-7f8 -- curl -sS \"http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz\"` -> green. Also see successful KMS decrypt in logs.
sree (sre): Queue drained to <5 tasks in 8m. No cert expirations missed. SLO looks back within target. :white_check_mark:
rachel (sec-eng): Thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) add a policy lint that checks alias patterns cover all deployed regions before merge; 2) add an RBAC post-change smoke that runs quick decrypts against a sampling of aliases. I'll draft PRs.
omar (infra): Also recommend we add a KMS-specific alert: sudden spike in kms:Decrypt DENY for any provisioner principal >5/min -> page oncall. Right now denies are only in dashboards.
rachel (sec-eng): Agreed. sree can you file an alert ticket?
sree (sre): Filed INFRA-8738: "KMS Decrypt DENY spike -> page oncall". Include runbook steps and SIEM query.
rachel (sec-eng): Great. Closing thread once runbook PRs are open. Thanks all. :lock:
